correctness.rationale: The exact state maps for the flags F00,F01,F10,F11 are derived by matching the newly attached leaf versus not; iterating pairs from {00,11} proves perfect matching iff b_(2j-1)!=b_(2j). Invertible adjacent-orientation differences give m-2 independent Bernoulli leaf increments conditional on this event, and Acan–Hitczenko’s proven caterpillar diameter identity completes the law. Finite exact independent inverter and matching-subset enumeration through order 14 checks all boundary flags and distribution counts; 41,003 actual checks pass. The induction, not the tests, establishes the infinite domain.

originality.rationale: The Acan–Hitczenko construction already proves the unbiased binary encoding and unconditional leaves/diameter; the genuinely new event characterization requires a matching-state recursion, after which the rare conditioned law yields the nontrivial 3/4 versus 1/2 diameter distinction. Janson treats permutation pattern occurrence laws, not perfect matchability. Mészáros proves general determinantal statements for uncovered vertices of maximum matchings on fixed trees, not an ensemble-specific matching feasibility law. Verified original source sections and close related results reveal no statement with equivalent scope. Remaining priority risk from unlocated broad caterpillar matching enumerations is explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: Perfect matching is a natural global feasibility property of sparse trees. Its probability \(2^{1-m}\) identifies an exponentially rare graph subclass whose leaf and diameter laws are completely different at linear scale: matched-conditioned diameter ratio \(\Delta_{2m}/(2m)\to 3/4\) instead of the unconditioned \(1/2\). The leaf-resolved matching probability gives a sharp monotone feasibility response across all possible leaf counts, so this is not an arbitrary slice or a routine unconditional statistic.
